title: Cloud Asset Inventory: finding what actually exists in the estate

videos.script: Terraform knows what it made. gcloud lists one kind of thing in one project. The console shows what someone clicks on. {{tools}} Cloud Asset Inventory is Google's own record of everything that exists, across the whole organisation. {{inventory}} Resources, IAM policies, organisation policies, and five weeks of history. {{contents}} Its API describes itself in a public document, and you can read that one with no credential at all. {{discovery}} A search names a scope, a query and the types of asset. Every topic in the company with no team label is one query. {{search}} Google refuses that query from the lab, at the method the document named. {{refusal}} Then the comparison that matters. You will apply Terraform for real, against the emulator, make one topic by hand, and find it. {{apply}} What exists, minus what is declared, is what someone forgot. {{end}}
